round1_fixes_verified.evidence: Task 1 now reads: '12-byte IV generated by SecureRandom; 128-bit GCM tag'
round1_fixes_verified.notes: Explicit and unambiguous. The class-level rationale (Architecture, line 16) also says 'Fresh 12-byte IV per encryption, 128-bit tag', and the unit test 'Fresh IV per call: encrypt(plaintext) called twice yields different IVs and different ciphertexts' (line 357) closes verification. round1_fixes_verified.fix: Exact 32-byte key check (missing / not valid hex / wrong length)
round1_fixes_verified.evidence: Task 1 reads: 'Constructor reads ${app.bot.token-encryption-key} and fails fast when the value is missing, not valid hex, or does not decode to exactly 32 bytes.' Unit tests (line 356) cover 'short key (<32 bytes), non-hex key, missing key — fail-fast with descriptive error at startup'.
round1_fixes_verified.notes: All three failure modes enumerated explicitly. AC at line 481 ties this to acceptance. Minor wording nit: the AC says 'wrong length' but Task 1 also covers 'not valid hex' — Task 1 description is the authoritative source for the implementer, so this is not a security gap.

round1_fixes_verified.evidence: D14: 'every Redis exception is logged at WARN (brute_bot_connect_redis_unavailable) AND a Micrometer counter botfunnel.bot_connect.brute_force.redis_failures is incremented'. Integration test 'Redis down — fail-open (AC11)' asserts: 'WARN log line emitted; Micrometer counter botfunnel.bot_connect.brute_force.redis_failures incremented'.
round1_fixes_verified.notes: Both the WARN and the metric are tied to an integration test scenario. Risk R9 (line 456) reflects the new observability. Sustained Redis outage will now surface in operations rather than silently degrade.

round1_fixes_verified.fix: bot_test_message_sent event explicitly NOT emitted in 06
round1_fixes_verified.evidence: D7 reads: 'No bot_test_message_sent audit event emitted — AC23 ties this event to each state change and in 06 the endpoint never produces a state change'. Alternative rejected: 'Emit bot_test_message_sent in 06 with success=false metadata — rejected (an event named sent with sent=false is a contradiction)'.
round1_fixes_verified.notes: Precise: no state change → no audit event in 06; 06b adds the event on the success branch. Avoids polluting audit log with semantically-incorrect events while still aligning with AC23 semantics. No security regression — audit-event truthfulness preserved.

round1_fixes_verified.fix: Telegram description scrubber for WARN logs
round1_fixes_verified.evidence: Task 2: 'Before any WARN log line that echoes a Telegram description field, run the value through a token-regex scrubber (\d{1,20}:[A-Za-z0-9_-]{30,50} → [REDACTED_TOKEN])'. Verify-smoke: 'scrubber unit test verifies a token-shaped substring is redacted'.
round1_fixes_verified.notes: The scrubber regex exactly matches the bean-validation regex on ConnectBotRequest.token (D16, line 250) — any string that passes validation will be redacted. Telegram getMe / setWebhook responses are the only places Telegram could echo a token, both covered. Minor non-finding suggestion: future-proof by applying the same scrubber on BotService-side WARN composition (e.g. Disconnect telegram-down at line 90) as belt-and-braces, but not required since BotService never composes log lines from Telegram description text.

round1_fixes_verified.fix: D14 INCR-every-attempt rationale (departure from AuthService shape)
round1_fixes_verified.evidence: D14 now states: 'This is an intentional departure from AuthService\'s INCR-on-failure-only shape: login has no equivalent succeed-then-bypass loop because a successful login terminates the per-email key explicitly.'
round1_fixes_verified.notes: Excellent rationale. Documents the divergence AND explains why it is correct (login terminates per-email key on success, eliminating bypass loop; Connect would have a bypass loop because Connect+Disconnect is freely repeatable). Prevents future maintainers from 'normalising' the counter back to AuthService shape and re-opening the bypass.

regression_check_per_project_unique_inde.summary: No security regressions introduced by D5/R4b (per-project partial unique index on bots).

checks_performed.check: Distinct error code (bot_already_in_project) does not leak cross-project information
checks_performed.reasoning: The new error code only fires when the requester's OWN project (verified via requireOwned at step 1) already has a connected bot. The signal exposes only state of a project the requester already owns. The platform-wide bot_already_connected signal (D1, R2) — which could theoretically leak existence of a foreign bot — is unchanged and remains mitigated by the generic-message stance documented at R2.

checks_performed.check: Compensating deleteWebhook is symmetric for the new race path
checks_performed.reasoning: Architecture (line 82) extends the compensating-deleteWebhook trigger to DuplicateKeyException from the per-project index: 'In both cases the exception is caught and mapped to the matching 409 — and triggers the same compensating deleteWebhook to roll back the setWebhook call from step 7.' R4b (line 451) confirms. No orphan-webhook risk from the new index path.

checks_performed.check: Index filter consistent (status=CONNECTED) and matches application invariant
checks_performed.reasoning: Both partial unique indexes use the same filter expression { status: 'CONNECTED' }. Disconnect (line 91) atomically sets status=DISCONNECTED, correctly clearing the index entry. AC at line 478 verifies both indexes exist with the correct filter. Integration test at line 386 covers the race-condition path.

checks_performed.check: DTOs unchanged — no new attack surface from per-project index
checks_performed.reasoning: BotResponse (line 307) carries only telegramBotId, telegramUsername, telegramFirstName, status, connectedAt — no project-identity field, no foreign-project metadata. D17 (no tokens round-trip) preserved. The new index changes Mongo schema only, not the API contract.

checks_performed.check: requireOwned remains the first step, preserving IDOR defence
checks_performed.reasoning: Connect pipeline (lines 58-79) runs requireOwned at step 1 BEFORE the per-project pre-check at step 3. A user cannot use the per-project pre-check (or its index counterpart) to probe foreign projects: requireOwned returns 404 first, never reaching step 3.

checks_performed.check: Rate-limit counter increments BEFORE per-project pre-check, no bypass via 409 enumeration
checks_performed.reasoning: Pipeline order: requireOwned → brute-force INCR → per-project pre-check → Telegram getMe → platform pre-check. An attacker probing 'is this project already taken?' via repeated 409s still increments the counter every attempt (D14), so the per-project signal cannot be enumerated past the threshold.

owasp_top10_recheck.A01_broken_access_control: Unchanged. requireOwned remains first step on every endpoint. New per-project index does not introduce any new authorization path.
owasp_top10_recheck.A02_cryptographic_failures: Strengthened. SecureRandom + 32-byte-exact key check both explicit in Task 1. AES-256-GCM with 12-byte IV + 128-bit tag remains correct.
owasp_top10_recheck.A03_injection: Unchanged. Bean-validation regex (D16) blocks malformed tokens at controller layer. New index does not introduce any new user-input → query path.
owasp_top10_recheck.A04_insecure_design: Improved. Race-condition design now symmetric for both uniqueness invariants. INCR-on-every-attempt rationale documented prevents future regressions. Scrubber design adds defence-in-depth against Telegram-echo token-leak.
owasp_top10_recheck.A05_security_misconfiguration: Unchanged. SecurityConfig untouched. .env.example placeholder + fail-fast on missing key.
owasp_top10_recheck.A07_auth_failures: Improved. Brute-force counter rationale + observability now explicit; Redis-outage visibility closes a previously-blind fail-open path.
owasp_top10_recheck.A08_software_data_integrity: Unchanged. Jackson @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true). No new deserialization surface.
owasp_top10_recheck.A09_security_logging_monitoring: Strengthened. Scrubber prevents token leak via Telegram-echo into WARN logs. Micrometer counter exposes brute-force-counter degradation. bot_test_message_sent correctly NOT emitted when no state change.
owasp_top10_recheck.A10_ssrf: Unchanged. Telegram base URL is configuration-driven (D12), not user-controlled. Webhook URL is computed from app.url + projectId, both server-side. No user-supplied URL reaches WebClient.

verdict_summary: All six round-1 minor findings are sufficiently addressed. The per-project unique index addition (D5/R4b) is symmetric with the existing platform-wide index design (D1/R4) and introduces no new security regressions across access control, information disclosure, rate-limiting, or compensating-action semantics. Approved.
